_comment: Federal wave F11 — first acts on empty poled keys. Coverage, not a flag flip. The census asked one question: which curated, directionally poled issue key holds no attributable federal act at all, and does a real 119th-Congress passage-form floor roll exist that would give it one? Twenty-two keys are empty and poled: twenty hold no federal act anywhere and two hold a Senate act and no House one. Two of the twenty are filled here. The other twenty, and both House-empty keys, are refused in writing below — twenty-two refusals, each with the measured reason.
_decidedBy: Federal wave F11, read against the Clerk's own paginated EVS indexes for 2025 and 2026 (657 House rolls), the Senate LIS vote menus for both sessions of the 119th (890 votes, 453 of them legislative), and the govinfo bill prints for every candidate that survived the title scan.
_doctrine: Formal record only. One instrument, one act. Fail-closed attribution. No party score, no package percentage, no invented stance, no floor moved.

Poleless and *_balance keys stay unread. That is doctrine, not a hole to patch: _rdSuppressedKey() runs before every wall, weight, lane and chamber check, and F11 adds no pole and proposes no *_balance pole. Twenty-eight keys are excluded as suppressed before the census ranks anything — the list is census.suppressedExcluded — and several of them hold no federal act anywhere either (civil_service_control, medical_freedom, tariffs_growth and immig_balance among them). None is a candidate here, and their emptiness is not counted as a gap: a suppressed key reads nothing whatever an act says about it.

A key with zero mapping rows cannot be priced by --reach at all: its KEY_UNIVERSE is the set of keys that already hold a mapping row. So the ranking had to come from the corpus and the chamber indexes together, and the seed records both sides of that join.

rankingMetric.asked: Rank the empty poled keys by how many members would become thin-readable from one full-weight passage-form floor vote.
rankingMetric.measured: --reach prices every fully-empty poled key at +102 in the Senate and +435 in the House, at n=1, with n=2 adding nothing. The ranking is therefore FLAT across all twenty-two: every one of them is worth an entire chamber and no more.
rankingMetric.consequence: So the ranking could not choose between them, and pretending it did would have been a fiction. What chooses is admissibility: does a real passage-form roll exist on an instrument whose text is that key's subject. Twenty-two candidates, two admissible, and the ordering among the twenty-two refusals is meaningless because they are all worth the same and all blocked on the same thing.
rankingMetric.whyOneActIsEnough: _rdLeanAllowed() returns true whenever floorActs > 0, so a single floor vote does not trip 'single_weak_act' and the row resolves as record_thin rather than staying empty. F10 measured n=1 equal to n=2 on all 78 in-play Senate keys and all 77 House keys. This wave does not require a second cousin to make a pattern, and did not look for one.

admitted.what: House roll 154 of the 119th Congress, 2nd session — On Passage of H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act (the 2026 Farm Bill). 30 April 2026. Passed 224-200, 0 Present, 6 Not Voting.
admitted.keyStateBefore: empty of federal acts. rural_ag held six mapping rows and no attributable federal act: five are Utah state bills (one of which, H.B. 114, carries a Utah roll that reaches state legislators only) and the sixth is H.R. 7567 itself, curated by wave F9 at w100 PRIMARY with no roll call attached. For every member of Congress the key read empty.
admitted.whyTheKeyWasEmpty: Not because the curation was missing. Because the ACT was. F9 read the bill, wrote five mapping rows including a w100 PRIMARY, and had no roll to hang them on — the House had not voted yet when F9 ran. F11 is the wave that supplies the vote.
admitted.instrumentIsStandalonePolicy: H.R. 7567 is the twelve-title farm bill reauthorization. It is not a continuing resolution, not an appropriations act, not an NDAA rider used as a proxy, not a special rule, not a Speaker election and not a discharge motion read as if it were passage. The question on roll 154 is On Passage of the bill itself.

textReadFromTheChamber.longTitle: To provide for the reform and continuation of agricultural and other programs of the Department of Agriculture through fiscal year 2031, and for other purposes.
textReadFromTheChamber.titles: I COMMODITIES · II CONSERVATION · III TRADE · IV NUTRITION · V CREDIT · VI RURAL DEVELOPMENT · VII RESEARCH, EXTENSION, AND RELATED MATTERS · VIII FORESTRY · IX ENERGY · X HORTICULTURE, MARKETING, AND REGULATORY REFORM · XI CROP INSURANCE · XII MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
textReadFromTheChamber.notATitleTrap: F10's four title traps were bills whose operative text pointed somewhere other than their names — weatherization that weatherized nothing, SWAPs that turned out to be State Wildlife Action Plans, SPACE that turned out to be shared federal office space, a screening 'mandate' that was a permissive sunset pilot. The test they yield is: search the print for the noun in its own name. This print says 'agricultur' 1,045 times, 'farm' 507, 'rural' 357, 'conservation' 289, 'forestry' 139, 'crop insurance' 43. Titles I, V, VI and XI are commodity supports, farm credit, rural development and crop insurance. The name and the instrument agree.

admitted.polarityFromTheText: yea_supports, already on file from F9 and unchanged here. The bill continues and reauthorizes commodity programs, farm credit, crop insurance and rural development through FY2031 — the rural_ag pole is 'Support family farms, ranchers and rural communities with fair prices and access', and continuing the programs that set reference prices and underwrite crop insurance is that. A nay is recorded as opposition to this bill, which is what a nay was.
admitted.weightEarnedByTheText: w100 PRIMARY, F9's weight, not revisited. Rule 25 asks why two similar instruments get different weights; the answer here is that there is no second instrument on this key to be inconsistent with. Four of twelve titles are the key's own subject and the long title names the Department of Agriculture. If a farm bill is not w100 on rural_ag then nothing is.

operativeSections: Sec. 204 — adds the new construction of affordable housing as an eligible CDBG activity, amending section 105(a) of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 (42 U.S.C. 5305(a)), capped at 20 percent of a recipient's allocation, and extends the low- and moderate-income requirement to new construction.

Sec. 212 — makes the Rental Assistance Demonstration permanent by striking 'until September 30, 2029' and inserting 'for fiscal year 2012 and each fiscal year thereafter', raises the unit cap from 455,000 to 555,000, and adds a mandatory tenant lease and management plan addendum for converted properties.

Sec. 405 (Choice in Affordable Housing Act) — amends section 8(o)(8) of the United States Housing Act of 1937 so that units in LIHTC-financed buildings satisfy Housing Choice Voucher inspection requirements, which is the operative barrier to landlord participation the bill's own title names.
Sec. 501 — reauthorizes the HOME Investment Partnerships Program and broadens income eligibility from 'low-income families' to households at or below 100 percent of area median family income.
Sec. 503 — gives McKinney-Vento homeless assistance recipients waiver authority over the section 415(b) expenditure limit for FY2027-2030.
textReadFromTheChamber.titleI: TITLE I--OPPORTUNITIES FOR HOUSING, one of twelve titles.
textReadFromTheChamber.shortTitle: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (Sec. 1(a) of the enrolled bill).
textReadFromTheChamber.longTitle: To increase the supply of housing in America, and for other purposes.

admitted.polarityFromTheText: yea_supports. The housing_support pole is 'Fund affordable housing and protect renters with assistance and limits on evictions'. Every section above funds affordable housing or extends renter assistance; a yea enacted them.
admitted.weightEarnedByTheText: w65, secondary, and the discount is the argument. Five operative sections amending permanent law plus one of twelve titles is real weight, not a mention. But the pole is a conjunction and the text only satisfies its first half: 'eviction' appears exactly twice in 442KB — once as an eligible use of manufactured-housing community grant funds ('eviction prevention') and once as a reporting metric in a data table — and neither is a limit on evictions. So the row is weighted for assistance and discounted for the half of the pole the text does not reach. w65 sits deliberately between this measure's permitting_reform w60 and its housing w80.
admitted.notRestuffing: The measure's existing rows are housing_build w100 PRIMARY ('loosen zoning and permitting so more homes can be built'), housing w80 PRIMARY ('boost supply and lower the cost to build and buy'), permitting_reform w60 and crypto_cbdc w40. Every one of those is the supply-and-zoning lane. housing_support is the subsidy-and-renter lane, and the vocabulary keeps them apart on purpose — a user can pick one without the other. The five sections named above are not the sections that earn housing_build its w100; they amend CDBG eligibility, the Rental Assistance Demonstration, section 8(o)(8) voucher inspections, the HOME program and McKinney-Vento. This is a subject the measure carries and no existing row reads, not a second reading of a subject already read.
admitted.howThisKeyNEARLYGOTREFUSED: The title-level census refused it. The enrolled short title is '21st Century ROAD to Housing Act' and the long title is 'To increase the supply of housing in America, and for other purposes' — neither contains 'affordable', 'renter', 'tenant', 'voucher' or 'rental assistance', and neither does the Clerk's title for House roll 224 or the Senate's for roll 53. A keyword scan of all 657 House rolls and 453 Senate legislative rolls of the 119th therefore returned ZERO candidates for housing_support and would have shipped a refusal. Only the enrolled print found the instrument. Runbook rule 43 — the name is not the instrument — cuts in the direction nobody had written down: a title scan can refuse a key that has an act.
admitted.membersNewlyReadable: 195 distinct members of Congress — 96 representatives and 99 senators — move from empty to record_thin on housing_support. Measured against the attributed rolls, not against the chamber headcount: the House roll carries 108 attributed members, not 435, so 96 is the honest figure and 435 would have been a fiction.

issues.rationale: Title I and five operative sections of the enrolled text are affordable-housing and renter assistance rather than supply: Sec. 204 adds new construction of affordable housing as an eligible CDBG activity (42 U.S.C. 5305(a)); Sec. 212 makes the Rental Assistance Demonstration permanent and raises its cap from 455,000 to 555,000 units with a mandatory tenant lease addendum; Sec. 405 amends section 8(o)(8) so LIHTC-financed units satisfy Housing Choice Voucher inspection, the operative barrier to landlord participation; Sec. 501 reauthorizes HOME and raises its income ceiling to 100 percent of area median; Sec. 503 gives McKinney-Vento recipients waiver authority over the expenditure limit. Weighted secondary at 65 rather than higher because the pole also asks for limits on evictions and the text has none — 'eviction' appears twice in the whole print, once as an eligible use of grant funds and once as a reporting metric. The measure's supply and zoning provisions are already read at housing_build w100 and housing w80; these sections are not those sections.

was.rationale: The bill's Sec. 10205 would have shielded pesticide makers from failure-to-warn suits; a bipartisan amendment struck it, so the enacted text does not include the shield.

retractions.why: The row's own rationale says the provision is not in the text, and the row's polarity says a yea opposes corporate accountability. Both cannot be true of the same vote. F9 wrote this as a note about what the bill WOULD have done, which was harmless while the measure had no roll call: with zero acts on the measure the row was inert and read to nobody. F11 lands the passage roll. The moment it lands, this row attributes to all 424 members who cast a side on roll 154 a position on a pesticide liability shield that the text they passed does not contain.
retractions.textBasis: Section-by-section diff of the two House prints. BILLS-119hr7567rh runs SEC. 10201 · 10202 · 10203 · 10204 · 10205 · 10206 · 10207 · 10211; BILLS-119hr7567eh — the print the House actually passed on roll 154 — runs SEC. 10201 · 10202 · 10203 · 10204 · 10211. Sections 10205 (pesticide-labeling uniformity), 10206 (authority of States) and 10207 (lawful use of authorized pesticides) are present in rh and absent from eh. The striking vote is H.Amdt. 196, House 119/2/148, adopted 280-142, which wave F9 ingested separately and recorded in its own migration header: 'H.Amdt. 196  119/2/148  280-142  states_federal_power  SEC. 10205, SEC. 10206 and SEC. 10207 struck from BILLS-119hr7567rh, absent from BILLS-119hr7567eh'. F9 found the same fact; it just had no roll on the parent, so nothing turned on it.
retractions.whyItIsSafeToRemove: econ_corp_account keeps ten mapping rows after the DELETE, four of them federal and three of those carrying acts: H.R. 6955 (w60, 2 rolls), H.R. 5376 (w60, 2 rolls) and S.J.Res. 18 (w75 PRIMARY, 2 rolls). The key does not go empty, does not lose its PRIMARY and does not lose an act. What it loses is a row that has never been read by anyone and, left in place, would be read wrongly by 424 people.
retractions.costDisclosed: MEASURED. Before the retraction, with roll 154 not yet ingested: 0 members read econ_corp_account through H.R. 7567, because measure 31 has no rollcall. After the retraction, with roll 154 ingested: still 0. The retraction costs exactly zero existing reads. Not retracting would have created 424 new reads on a provision that is not in the passed text — 209 Republican yeas plus 14 Democratic yeas recorded as opposing corporate accountability, and 197 Democratic nays plus 3 Republican nays recorded as supporting it, on the strength of three struck sections. That is the whole cost of this wave's retraction column: nothing lost, 424 wrong reads not published.

was.rationale: Secs. 10206–10207 would have limited state label authority and preempted local pesticide rules; both were struck by the same bipartisan amendment.

retractions.why: The same defect, named in the row's own words: 'would have', 'both were struck'. The two sections this row reads are SEC. 10206 and SEC. 10207, and the passed print does not contain either. Landing roll 154 would tell 424 members they took a position on state label authority and local pesticide preemption in a bill whose text is silent on both.
retractions.textBasis: The same eh-versus-rh section diff and the same H.Amdt. 196 (119/2/148, 280-142) recorded above.
retractions.whyItIsSafeToRemove: This one is NOT free, and the seed says so rather than burying it. H.R. 7567 is property_rights' only federal mapping row; the other seven are Utah state bills. After the DELETE property_rights holds no federal instrument at all, so it moves out of the 37 poled keys that have a House instrument and no Senate one and into the group that has neither — the count of poled keys with no federal instrument anywhere goes 20 -> 21. Its Utah PRIMARY (H.B. 289, w55) and its four Utah rolls are untouched, so no state legislator loses a read. The trade is stated plainly: F11 makes one federal coverage number worse in order not to publish 424 attributions the text cannot support. A key that reads empty is honest; a key that reads a struck section is not.
retractions.costDisclosed: MEASURED. Before: 0 members of Congress read property_rights through H.R. 7567 (measure 31 has no rollcall) and 0 read it through any other federal measure — the key has zero federal acts either way. census._method: Two metrics, measured against the live corpus, not recalled from F10's table. METRIC A is the brief's own phrasing — a poled key with no federal mapping row at all in that chamber. refusals.why: H.R. 692 (China Exchange Rate Transparency Act) directs the United States Executive Director at the IMF to advocate for exchange-rate transparency — it imposes no tariff and changes no rate. H.R. 881 (DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act) is a federal contracting and grant restriction. H.R. 747 (Stop Chinese Fentanyl Act) directs a strategy and a report. None of the three is a tariff, and the pole is 'Use tariffs to counter China and unfair trade practices' — the instrument has to be a tariff. The two Senate passage-form candidates, S.J.Res. 49 and S.J.Res. 88, ARE tariff instruments, but they terminate a national emergency under which global tariffs were imposed; their operative subject is the President's emergency authority and their scope is global, not China. Mapping them here would require yea_opposes on a resolution about who may impose a tariff rather than about whom a tariff counters. The axis those two actually belong to is tariffs_authority, which the corpus deliberately holds at no pole, and F11 adds no pole — that fact is stated second, after the textual reason, per runbook rule 42.
refusals.blockedOn: a passage-form vote on an instrument that actually imposes or removes a China-specific tariff

refusals.measured: House 6 rolls touching the subject, all 6 passage-form; Senate 12 touching, 5 passage-form. Read all of them.
refusals.why: Five of the six House candidates and all five Senate ones are Congressional Review Act disapprovals of Bureau of Land Management resource management plans (H.J.Res. 104, 105, 106, 130, 140). A CRA disapproval nullifies a federal agency's plan and leaves the decision with Congress and the agency; it transfers nothing to a state or a county. The pole is 'Transfer more federal land decisions to states and county governments', and Congress overriding its own executive branch is not that transfer — it is the federal government deciding twice. H.J.Res. 140 is already in the corpus at lands_preserve w90 PRIMARY yea_opposes and lands_energy w75, which is the reading its text supports. The sixth House candidate, H.R. 3187, conveys one named parcel of Forest Service property; a single property transaction is not a transfer of land decision-making authority.

_findings: RULE 43 CUTS BOTH WAYS. The name is not the instrument, and F10 wrote that rule to catch bills whose titles promise more than their text delivers. F11 found the inverse on the same day: a title scan of all 657 House and 453 Senate legislative rolls of the 119th returned ZERO candidates for housing_support, and the key had an act the whole time. Both of this wave's housing findings come from one print — H.R. 6644 earns housing_support on five operative sections and is refused for housing_first_time on three permissive pilots — which is the cleanest available demonstration that the test is the text and never the title, in either direction.

A ROLL IS NOT FREE. Landing one act made five pre-existing mapping rows readable, not one. Two of them read sections that the passed text does not contain and had to be retracted; one arrives correctly and is disclosed rather than claimed; one stays suppressed because it is a *_balance key. A coverage wave that counts only the row it argued for understates its own footprint by four rows.

THE RANKING WAS INERT. The brief asked for the empty poled keys ranked by members newly thin-readable from one full-weight passage-form vote. --reach prices every one of them identically (+435 House, +102 Senate, n=1 equal to n=2), so the ranking is a flat tie across all 22 and the real discriminator is whether an admissible instrument exists. Reported as a flat tie instead of as an ordering.

--reach CANNOT SEE AN EMPTY KEY. Its KEY_UNIVERSE is the set of keys that already hold at least one mapping row, so the five poled keys with zero rows anywhere are outside the instrument that was supposed to price them. The census had to be built from direct SQL against vr_measure_issues and vr_rollcalls cross-matched against the scraped chamber indexes. Recorded as a limitation of the tool, not worked around silently.

--reach IS A PRE-WAVE INSTRUMENT AND CANNOT MEASURE THE WAVE THAT PASSES IT. The brief asked for `--reach` on the poled empty keys, and the honest answer is that the flag's own numbers are identical before and after this wave. Measured: `--set all --waves f1,f2,f3,f4,f10 --reach` and `--set all --waves f1,f2,f3,f4,f10,f11 --reach` produce output that differs in exactly two lines, both of them the header naming the wave list. Not one figure moves. The cause is structural rather than a bug: the --reach branch of scripts/vr-federal-fpi.mjs builds every count from `winB` and `before` (the database as it stands) and from `lane`, and never touches `V.lane` / `after`, which is where a wave's projected rows live. So the wave list argument reaches the header and nothing else. Two consequences worth writing down. First, --reach prices a hypothetical: what the best instrument that could ever exist would convert against the current corpus, which is a planning number and not a result. Second, it counts UNREAD ROWS — rows that exist and are suppressed — so a wave like this one, which creates READS rather than unread rows, is invisible to it by construction: rural_ag and housing_support both still print unread 0 with a ceiling of a whole chamber, before and after. The wave's actual movement had to be measured with `--json` gainedReads/lostReads, which is a genuine before/after pair over the same engine. Recorded so the next wave does not quote a --reach table as evidence that it shipped something.

A MIRROR IS NOT THE MAPPING — THE GATE THAT FAILED WAS READING HALF ITS SOURCE. scripts/test-vr-vote-seed.mjs refused this wave's vote seed with 'measure H.R. 7567 (119th) has no mapping in db/vr-issue-seed.json and is not declared in measuresDeliberatelyUnmapped'. The bill is mapped: five rows written by netlify/database/migrations/20260721100000_seed_farm_bill_2026.sql, of which three survive this wave, including the rural_ag w100 PRIMARY that is the entire product here. What is true is only that none of the five was ever mirrored into db/vr-issue-seed.json — which runbook rule 20 says is not a defect, because applyCuratedIssueSeed() upserts only the keys the mirror carries and an omitted key is a live row left alone. Three doors were open and two of them were refused. Declaring the bill in measuresDeliberatelyUnmapped would have put a false sentence in the permanent record — that door exists for a measure read in full and refused every candidate key, which is H.R. 1069 and F7's seven Iran resolutions, all of them carrying no issue rows at all. Mirroring the bill's three surviving rows would have been true but wrong-shaped: rule 20 makes a mirrored key owe its live rationale byte for byte, and these three sit alongside two rows this very migration deletes, so the mirror would have been written against text in motion; and scripts/test-vr-federal-roster-r2.mjs pins db/vr-issue-seed.json unchanged, so a coverage wave would have broken an identity wave's discipline list to pass its own gate. The third door was to fix the gate's source, and that is what shipped: it now reads the migrations for the same fact, per file (variable names repeat across files, and the concatenated blob would let one file's m_farm satisfy another's insert) and per (measure, key) pair minus the pairs a later migration DELETEs. The widening is measured, not asserted: across all seventeen vote seeds it admits H.R. 7567 and nothing else, the eight measures behind the declinedFacets door stay behind it, the mirror is still consulted first, and a variable the parser cannot bind is credited to nothing. Recorded as runbook rule 51, and pinned in section 10b of scripts/test-vr-federal-wave-f11.mjs against the source so a later widening fails loudly.

F10 RESERVED THE STAMP AND ITS SUITE ASSERTED THE STAMP WAS EMPTY. F10's seed says 20261028000000 is 'recorded here and not consumed, so the next wave takes it'; its suite then required MIGS.filter(f => f.startsWith('20261028')).length === 0. Both sentences were right on the day F10 shipped and they cannot both survive the wave that accepts the offer. F11 consumed the stamp, as this brief directs, and F10's suite failed on it. The assertion was narrowed rather than removed, to what F10 can still honestly claim: at most one file at that stamp, not carrying F10's name, and declared by some db/vr-federal-mapping-seed-*.json. Every one of F10's no-write claims is untouched — rowsShipped 0, migrationsWritten 0, voteSeedsWritten 0, measures[] empty, promotes[] empty, retractions[] empty — and the suite passes at 250 checks. Recorded as runbook rule 52.
